video_title: Lakers SWEPT + Will Thunder Go UNDEFEATED In Playoffs?!? [Reupload]

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Donovan Mitchell's historic 39-point second half
quotes.quote: It's just unbelievable, obviously historic second half. The fact that when his team needed him the most, when, you know, season on the line, to down 2-1 and he kind of puts the team on his back 39 in a half after struggling a little bit in the first half was outrageous. And this is the format for them to be really good. This is why they went and got a James Harden who's this consistent, solid, didn't turn the ball over. I think he only had like two turnovers, 24 and 11, was efficient, got to the free throw line. This version of the Cavs offense is so dangerous and so potent. But Donovan Mitchell, man, he was unbelievable in the second half. And I always wonder when teams go on runs like this, Lou, like 22-0, like the Lakers last night, 25-0 run. How do you not get to like the free throw line or Cade Cunningham? How do you not do something to try and stop?

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Donovan Mitchell's mindset to score 39 points in the second half
quotes.quote: The game is literally dependent on it, right? And so you just evaluate everything. Being a scorer myself, if I'm having a slow half, I start to make my adjustments. I start to think where is the game going for me? Is this a facilitator night? Is this a night where I need to be more aggressive or do I just need to crash out and just start being aggressive and just getting shots up at the rim? Because once you see one go in, you feel like you can score in bunches. And Donovan Mitchell is one of those type of guys. When he starts to get momentum, that opens up three levels of scoring for him. Mid-range, three-pointer, getting to the rim. Actually opens up four because he's able to get to the free throw line as well. When you start seeing that ball go in, the rim becomes like an ocean and you can just do anything on the floor. And I think that was the adjustment that he made in the second half. Just start playing with confidence. He was able to get a floater to go. Look where he's at. I'm eight feet from the rim right here. Now, my legendary step through, my signature move. I'm stepping through, I'm attacking. I'm not settling. I'm getting to the rim. That's another floater. I'm another seven, eight feet from the rim. Now what that opens up? Opens up the three-point line. Now we can dance out on the perimeter. So once you start seeing a guy attack the rim, getting five to ten feet from the rim, seeing a couple of those go, getting to the free throw line. Now that opens up everything and now you're confident and you can go off for a 39-point second half like he did.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Donovan Mitchell's 'heat check' scoring ability
quotes.quote: I don't know about on the list. There's so many different guys that when they get going and like Lou said, it's just a feeling as a as a shooter, as a scorer, where the hoop just feels this big and everything you throw at the rim is going in. You just get the craziest momentum and the craziest heat checks. We've seen Steph Curry do it. We've seen Luka do it. Anthony Edwards. SGA. There are so many different scorers that just obviously get hot and there's no stopping. Especially like Lou just said, Donovan Mitchell, he was hitting threes, he was breaking you off on ISO, he was getting to the rim, he shot 15 free throws. This was the most balanced kind of scoring offensive check that I've had seen them do in a long time.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Cade Cunningham's turnover issues and team adjustments
quotes.quote: I think he's asked to do his job, but you got to give Cleveland that credit, right? Like I just talked about Donovan Mitchell crashing out. Think about Max Strus, right? Like think about him. He's known as a shooter, he's known as a guy that's going to extend their offense to the three-point line and that's what makes them dangerous. But in this playoff series, he's just decided I'm going to be a defensive disruptor and I'm just going to make it difficult for Cade Cunningham. Now, I'm not saying he's a lockdown defender and he's locking him up one-on-one, but he's doing a tremendous job of junking up the game. Him and Schroder, trapping him, picking them up full court. They've they're forcing turnovers from out-of-bounds plays. Just being in the way and making everything that he's going to do difficult, knowing that in this series now, we know that he's going to be a ball-dominant guy. His impact is going to be with the ball in his hands. So let's make it as difficult as we can. And I think he and Schroder have done an exceptional job of just turning them over, catching them on the sidelines. Every time I've seen Cade Cunningham on the sideline, they're running guys at him, they're trapping him, they're using the sideline as a third defender. When he's taking the ball out or if he's the guy getting the basketball up up the court, boxing one type vibes, AAU vibes, making it where he can't catch the ball. Or if he is going to catch the ball, we're going to catch him on the sideline. Those guys have done a great job of just junking up the game and making it difficult for Cade. So are are they asking him to do too much? No, this is his job, but they also have to adjust. Make him catch the ball, have him catch the ball at half court. Have him on a dribble handoff. Use some of these other guys to bring the basketball up to initiate the offense. That's an adjustment JB has to make as as the coach of this team. But he's not asked to do too much. This is what he does.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams

Damn, I could be up 3-1. We can be in a better position if we clean up some of these things that we've already known we're going to be issues for us. And I think the momentum has to go towards Detroit being at home with the success they've had there and the the not success that the Cavs have had on the road. So like they're still in a fine situation. It's just when you have an offense like that and your team is is determined based on your defense, your toughness, you can't turn the ball over like that. You have to get shots at the basket. It's kind of it's it's one of those things, Chandler, where you're sitting there two and two, and you you're in pretty decent position, but you get home in your bed, you're like, damn, I could be up 3-1 if I if I take care of the basketball. Damn, I could be up 3-1. We can be in a better position if we clean up some of these things that we've already known we're going to be issues for us. So that's where that that's where that part comes in. Like, is he careless with the basketball? Yes, but at the end of the day, who else is going to do it on the Detroit Pistons?
